Ever booted up that old PC, just to realize you've forgotten the password? Well, there's a pretty easy way around it. It involves booting from a Windows installation CD, gaining access to a command prompt, and replacing OSK.exe (On Screen Keyboard) with CMD.exe. Then from the login screen, attempt to open the on screen keyboard and BAM! You've got yourself a command prompt with System Rights and you're now able to change the password of any user on the machine.

You'll Need:

  • Access to the Boot order of the machine
  • A Windows installation CD/thumb-drive/other bootable device
  • A Brain

How it's done

Boot the machine from the installation CD, choose your language, click next until you have the option to Repair or Fix or Recover, then select Command Prompt.

Now it's time to replace the On-Screen-Keyboard with the command prompt executable.

First we need to find the drive that windows is installed on. It's usually C:/ but not always.

Type this to list all the drives:

wmic logicaldisk get caption

Now that you've found the correct drive, backup OSK.exe, just in case one wants to use the OSK in the future:

copy C:\Windows\system32\osk.exe C:\Windows\system32\osk.old

Then delete OSK.exe:

del C:\Windows\system32\osk.exe

And then create a new Command Prompt executable with the name osk.exe:

copy C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe C:\Windows\system32\osk.exe

Alright, now boot into windows and bring up the On-Screen-Keyboard, but instead, a command prompt with SYSTEM rights will open up.

Now we need to change a password. Hopefully you know the username of the account which password you want to change but here is how you list all the users on the machine:

net user

Pick the account which password you want to change. For this guide, i'll use the admin account.

The command looks like this:

net user USER_NAME NEW_PASSWORD

So, to change the password of the admin account, we type this:

net user Administrator password123

And there you go, the password of the user Administrator is now password123

We can now close the command prompt and login.

MISSION ACCOMPLISHED
Interesting way to change the password of any user, at the Windows login screen.
